principles.title: Protein first, always
principles.summary: Aim for 1.6–2.2g of protein per kg of bodyweight per day.
principles.detail: Protein is the only macro directly tied to muscle repair. Spread it across 3–4 meals rather than one big serving — your body can only use so much at once for muscle synthesis. Good sources: chicken breast, eggs, Greek yogurt, lentils, tofu, whey isolate.

principles.title: Match calories to your goal
principles.summary: Surplus to build muscle, deficit to lose fat, maintenance to recomp.
principles.detail: A surplus of 200–300 calories a day supports lean muscle gain without excess fat. A deficit of 300–500 calories a day is sustainable for fat loss without losing muscle or crashing your energy. Track for two weeks before adjusting — day-to-day weight swings are mostly water.

principles.title: Carbs are fuel, not the enemy
principles.summary: Time your carbs around training for the best energy and recovery.
principles.detail: Eat the bulk of your carbs in the 3 hours before and after training. Whole sources — oats, rice, potatoes, fruit — digest predictably and refill glycogen better than processed sugar, which spikes and crashes.

principles.title: Don't cut fat too low
principles.summary: Keep fats at 20–30% of total calories for hormone health.
principles.detail: Testosterone and estrogen production both depend on dietary fat. Going much below 20% of calories from fat for an extended period is linked to hormone disruption and poor recovery, even if the scale moves faster short-term.

principles.title: Hydration affects performance more than people think
principles.summary: A 2% drop in hydration can measurably reduce strength output.
principles.detail: Aim for 3–4 liters a day, more on heavy training days or in heat. If your urine is darker than pale straw, you're behind on fluids before you even start your session.

principles.title: Meal timing matters less than total intake
principles.summary: Hitting your daily totals matters more than exact meal timing.
principles.detail: Intermittent fasting, 6 small meals, or 3 big meals — all work if your daily protein and calorie totals are right. Pick the pattern that fits your schedule and that you can actually stick to for months, not days.

safety.title: Avoid extreme calorie deficits
safety.detail: Cutting more than 1000 calories below maintenance risks muscle loss, fatigue, and a slowed metabolism. If a plan promises rapid fat loss in days, it's selling water weight and burnout, not real progress.

safety.title: Check with a doctor before big changes
safety.detail: If you have any existing condition — diabetes, heart issues, kidney concerns, or you're pregnant — talk to a physician before starting a new diet or supplement, especially anything involving fasting or high-protein intake.

safety.title: Supplements support a diet, they don't replace one
safety.detail: No powder fixes a bad diet. Whole food should make up the large majority of your intake; supplements fill small, specific gaps — protein totals, creatine, a multivitamin if your diet is genuinely limited.

safety.title: Fatigue and dizziness are signals, not weakness
safety.detail: Persistent fatigue, dizziness, hair loss, or missed periods are signs of under-eating, not signs you need to push harder. Scale back and reassess rather than pushing through.

safety.title: Don't overcorrect on water either
safety.detail: Drinking far more water than you need, especially without electrolytes, can dilute sodium levels dangerously. More is not always better — balance is the goal, not maximum volume.

foodsToFavor.name: Chicken breast
foodsToFavor.why: Lean protein with minimal fat, versatile for every meal.

foodsToFavor.name: Eggs
foodsToFavor.why: Complete protein with all essential amino acids, cheap and fast to cook.

foodsToFavor.name: Greek yogurt
foodsToFavor.why: High protein-to-calorie ratio plus gut-friendly probiotics.

foodsToFavor.name: Oats
foodsToFavor.why: Slow-digesting carbs that keep energy steady through a session.

foodsToFavor.name: Sweet potatoes
foodsToFavor.why: Complex carbs with fiber and potassium for muscle function.

foodsToFavor.name: Salmon
foodsToFavor.why: Protein plus omega-3 fats that support joint and heart health.

foodsToFavor.name: Leafy greens
foodsToFavor.why: Micronutrients and fiber with almost no calorie cost.

foodsToFavor.name: Almonds & walnuts
foodsToFavor.why: Healthy fats and protein in a portable, shelf-stable snack.

foodsToFavor.name: Lentils & beans
foodsToFavor.why: Plant protein and fiber that keeps you full for hours.

foodsToFavor.name: Berries
foodsToFavor.why: Lower-sugar fruit option, high in antioxidants.

foodsToLimit.name: Sugary drinks & soda
foodsToLimit.why: Large calorie load with zero nutritional return and a fast energy crash.

foodsToLimit.name: Deep-fried foods
foodsToLimit.why: High in inflammatory fats that slow recovery between sessions.

foodsToLimit.name: Refined white bread & pastries
foodsToLimit.why: Spikes blood sugar fast, leaves you hungry again within the hour.

foodsToLimit.name: Excess alcohol
foodsToLimit.why: Directly suppresses muscle protein synthesis for up to 24 hours after drinking.

foodsToLimit.name: Processed deli meats
foodsToLimit.why: High sodium and preservatives; swap for fresh-cooked lean meats where possible.
